chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a corpse is found in a wilderness area, its blood money (diyah) is paid from the public treasury, for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'The blood of a Muslim man shall not be invalidated.'
ai.seo_question: Who pays the blood money for an unidentified corpse found in the wilderness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'diyah al-murafa' (blood money for the unknown), assigning financial liability to the public treasury (bayt al-mal) for unidentified corpses found in wilderness areas. It grounds this legal mechanism in the prophetic tradition of Imam Ali (peace be upon him), emphasizing the preservation of a Muslim's honor and status even when their identity is lost. This ruling highlights the state's role in ensuring justice and preventing the neglect of the deceased's rights within the Shia jurisprudential framework.
